title: udlm_provenance — the modification chain
description:
What changed on this write, field by field: the source kind, the previous value, and DUAL ATTRIBUTION — the policy that applied the value and the pinned layer that supplied it.

WHY BOTH ATTRIBUTIONS. `source` answers who decided; `via_layer` answers where the value came from. They are routinely different — a policy selects a value a layer carried — and collapsing them loses the ability to ask either question: change the layer and you cannot tell which decisions consumed it; change the policy and you cannot tell what it was choosing between.

THIS IS A HISTORY CLAIM, WHICH IS WHY IT LIVES HERE. The working record makes state claims only; only a sealed, chained, anchored record may be cited as lineage (ADR-059). The record's own `provenance` block is readable and not citable — this is the citable one.

_schemaURL.description: OpenLineage: the schema defining this facet. Pinned to this file — a facet whose schema URL points elsewhere is a different facet wearing the same name, and the name is all a consumer has to go on.

modifications.description: One entry per field this write touched, in application order.

source_kind.description: Which class of writer set it (data-model-core §6/§7). The same vocabulary the record's provenance block uses, so the two are comparable rather than merely similar.

previous_value.description: What it was. Absent means the field was unset — which is distinct from a null previous value, and the distinction is what tells a reader whether this write created the field or changed it.

via_layer.description: The pinned layer that SUPPLIED the value — where it came from. Pinned, so the value is re-derivable at the version that produced it.
